reasoning:
Finding: "x402 SettlementBook key uses the raw nonce string, so re-casing the nonce re-spends a redeemed payment on another route or target". At e4b6da3, acceptX402 (src/payments/serverSide.ts:283-289) now checks that the nonce matches NONCE = /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/ (line 220). A non-string or malformed nonce gets 400 malformed_payment. A valid nonce is lower-cased before the book key `x402:${getAddress(from)}:${nonce}` is built. The same canonical nonce is passed to settleX402 and used as the railReference (`const ref = nonce`). authorizationState now builds its query with URLSearchParams from the getAddress'd authorizer and the canonical nonce. x402Flights is also keyed on the canonical key, so concurrent presentations with different letter cases are serialised. The sim facilitator (src/payments/sim/facilitator.ts) now keys usedNonces with nonceKey(), which lower-cases the nonce, so the sim models the chain.

Reproduction: I used throwaway worktrees at e4b6da3 and b6304b7, both since removed. The regression test is "a re-cased x402 nonce is the same payment: refused on another route and another prefix target, never charged twice", added at test/proxy.test.ts:294. It buys x402 for /v1/a and presents it (200), then presents the re-cased nonce on /v1/b with the resource rewritten and expects 402 BOUND_ELSEWHERE. It runs the same check for a prefix target (berlin to hamburg) and checks that malformed nonces get 400. It passes on e4b6da3. Copied into the b6304b7 tree, it fails at proxy.test.ts:300 with expected 402, actual 200, which is the original bug. The full proxy suite on e4b6da3 passes 26/26.

Variants I tried on e4b6da3, all now correct:
- Alternating mixed-case nonce plus a lower-cased `from` on route b: 402, 1 charge, 1 upstream hit.
- Concurrent first presentation, with the original on a, the re-cased nonce on b and the original on b: exactly one 200, 1 charge, 1 hit.
- Re-cased nonce presented first on a, then the original on b: 402.

Other schemes: the L402 key uses paymentHash from an HMAC-verified macaroon, so it cannot be re-cased without breaking verification. The card-psp id is restricted to /^pi_\w+$/ and resolved by exact match at the PSP (sim psp.ts:178). This matches real PSPs, which treat ids case-sensitively, so a re-cased id finds no intent and is refused 402 (unknown payment intent). No open variants found.

Minor note: two leftover worktrees from another auditor (/tmp/audit-v2proxy-new and /tmp/audit-v2proxy-old) are still registered. They are not mine, so I left them.
evidence: src/payments/serverSide.ts:220 `const NONCE = /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/;`; serverSide.ts:287-289 `if (typeof raw !== "string" || !NONCE.test(raw)) throw ...; nonce = raw.toLowerCase(); key = `x402:${getAddress(...from)}:${nonce}`;`; serverSide.ts:291-294 x402Flights keyed on canonical key; settleX402 `const ref = nonce`; authorizationState uses `new URLSearchParams({ authorizer: getAddress(from), nonce })`. src/payments/sim/facilitator.ts nonceKey() lower-cases the nonce in verify, settle and /authorization-state. Regression test test/proxy.test.ts:294 passes on e4b6da3 (suite 26/26 pass). On b6304b7 src with the new test file it fails at test/proxy.test.ts:300: expected 402, actual 200. Ad-hoc variant tests (mixed case plus lower-cased from, concurrent cross-route presentations, re-cased first then original) all pass on e4b6da3, each with 1 charge and 1 upstream hit.

variantsStillOpen: Timeout or 5xx after the upstream already did the work: a POST that times out (or gets a 5xx) is classed as 'transient' (outcomeOf, paymentProxy.ts:56-59). The credential stays usable, so the buyer can POST again with a different body. Reproduced with upstreamTimeoutMs=200, an upstream that takes 400ms, and card-psp: r1=502, r2=200, upstream.bodies=[job0,job1], card-psp charges=3 (one payment, two jobs run).

Upstream 4xx (e.g. 422) on a POST is 'refused'. It neither consumes the credential nor marks it delivered, so a buyer can send any number of different bodies until one gets a 2xx. Reproduced: statuses 422,422,422,200,402, with 4 upstream hits on one x402 payment. Low impact if the upstream does no billable work on a 4xx.

The deliveries map in SettlementBook is in memory only (serverSide.ts:121). After a proxy restart, a consumed POST credential has delivered=false again, so it can deliver once more. This fits the documented in-memory limitation of the book, but it is an open gap for non-GET routes.
reasoning: Finding: "Re-presenting a settled credential on a non-GET paid route runs the paid action again with a new body: one payment buys unlimited POSTs". The fix in e4b6da3 adds SettlementBook.tryStartDelivery(key, repeatable) (src/payments/serverSide.ts:179-185). It returns 'consumed' when a non-repeatable payment has already delivered, and 'busy' while a delivery is in flight. The check and the start happen synchronously, with no await between them. The proxy's paid() calls it with SAFE_METHODS.has(method) (src/proxy/paymentProxy.ts:54 SAFE_METHODS={GET,HEAD}; :193-199). On 'consumed' it answers 402 credential_consumed; on 'busy' it answers 409. deliver() no longer calls deliveryStarted itself (:209-211). The method comes from the request and is upper-cased (:156). Routes must match the configured method (routes.ts:112-113), so a POST route cannot be reached with GET to dodge the check. GET bodies are dropped in forward.ts:73, so on GET routes the binding (path+query) covers all of the input. I reran the original scenario on e4b6da3. For all three schemes, the second POST with a new body gets 402 credential_consumed and never reaches the upstream, with one charge per credential. Concurrent POSTs give exactly one 200. PUT, DELETE and PATCH each give 200 then 402. A re-cased x402 nonce, or a different query string, on a consumed POST is refused (402). The fix holds for the reported scenario. Remaining variants all come from the 'transient' and 'refused' outcomes, which keep the credential usable. The most serious is a timeout or 5xx after the upstream already did the work: a retry with a new body runs a second job on the same payment.

variantsStillOpen: Not this finding's code path, but the same kind of leak: other providers send their key over plain http with no check when the user writes an explicit http:// base URL. At e4b6da3, LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible with LLM_BASE_URL=http://ollama.com/v1 and LLM_API_KEY, openai with OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://api.example.com/v1, and anthropic with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://api.example.com all build an adapter without complaint. Only OllamaAdapter has the https-or-loopback guard.

Wrong result but no leak: a bare IPv4-mapped loopback address (OLLAMA_HOST=::ffff:127.0.0.1) is not treated as loopback and becomes https://[::ffff:7f00:1], so a local plain-http server cannot be reached. It fails safe.
reasoning: Finding: "OLLAMA_API_KEY sent as a Bearer token over plain HTTP when OLLAMA_HOST has no scheme". At b6304b7, ollamaHost() in src/llm/config.ts (around line 96) put http:// in front of any OLLAMA_HOST that had no scheme, and OllamaAdapter.post() then sent `authorization: Bearer <key>`. At e4b6da3 there are two layers of protection. (1) src/llm/config.ts:96-100 now calls ollamaBaseUrl() (src/llm/providers/ollama.ts, added at about lines 55-79). It picks http only for loopback or private hosts (isPrivateHost) and picks https for public hosts or port 443; an explicit scheme is kept as written, and any scheme other than http or https is a config error. (2) The OllamaAdapter constructor (ollama.ts, about lines 95-105) throws LlmError('config') when an apiKey is set and the URL is neither https nor loopback (isLoopbackHost). Because that check is in the constructor, it also covers an explicit http://, LAN hosts, LLM_BASE_URL and adapters built directly in code. I ran a reproduction script through llmConfigFromEnv and createLlm, with both OLLAMA_API_KEY and LLM_API_KEY. At b6304b7, OLLAMA_HOST=ollama.com gave http://ollama.com and ollama.com:443 gave http://ollama.com:443, and an adapter was created both times, so the key would go out in cleartext. At e4b6da3 both give https://ollama.com. I tried about 20 other spellings: http://ollama.com, HTTP://, 192.168.1.20, ollama.lan, decimal and hex IP forms (134744072, 0x08080808, which resolve to https://8.8.8.8), [::ffff:8.8.8.8]:80, localhost.ollama.com, user@host, a path suffix, padding spaces, and LLM_BASE_URL without a scheme. Each one either became https or was refused with kind=config. The only plain-http URLs that still take a key are true loopback addresses (127.x, the 2130706433 form, foo.localhost, 0 → 0.0.0.0), which the fix allows on purpose. The /api/tags probe in compare.ts (line 179) sends no key. The only related gap I found is that other providers have no such check when the user writes an explicit http:// URL. That is a different code path and a deliberate configuration choice, so I list it as a variant rather than a failure of this fix.

reasoning:
Finding: "Schema validator ignores additionalProperties:false for keys that exist on Object.prototype". I reproduced it on b6304b7. validateJson({statements:[],unrecognized:[],constructor:'x',toString:5}, INTERPRETATION_SCHEMA) returned [], so the object passed as valid. "__proto__" was also accepted, as was a required key that is only inherited ("valueOf"). The strict path (toStrictSchema/fromStrict) and nested objects let these keys through too.

Commit e4b6da3 adds an `own()` helper based on Object.hasOwn (src/llm/jsonSchema.ts:40). validateJson uses it for the properties lookup (:82), and the required check now uses Object.hasOwn (:80). fromStrict uses own() (:131) and writes keys with defineProperty, so a "__proto__" key stays an ordinary key and does not change the prototype (:134).

On e4b6da3, all of these cases are now rejected. That covers the root of INTERPRETATION_SCHEMA, the strict schema and fromStrict followed by validation, nested additionalProperties:false objects, and inherited required keys. A property that is actually declared with a prototype name, such as "constructor", still validates.

I tried related variants and none still produce a wrong result:
- The additionalProperties-as-schema branch already behaved correctly.
- stripNulls (src/grounding/llmInterpreter.ts:97) uses Object.fromEntries, which creates own properties, so a "__proto__" key cannot pollute the prototype.
- `"const" in s` (:66) reads the schema, not model output.

The regression test is at test/llm.test.ts:115. Run against b6304b7's src, it fails ("not ok", actual [] where `$: unexpected property "constructor"` was expected). On e4b6da3 it passes, and so does the whole llm.test.ts (33 pass, 0 fail).
evidence:

- Old (b6304b7): A=[] for constructor/toString, B=[] for __proto__, C=[] for required "valueOf", D=[] and E=[] for "hasOwnProperty" on the strict path, G=[] for nested "constructor".
- New (e4b6da3): A gives `$: unexpected property "constructor"` and `"toString"`; B gives `unexpected property "__proto__"`; C gives `missing required property "valueOf"`; D and E give `unexpected property "hasOwnProperty"`; G gives `$.a: unexpected property "constructor"`.

Fix locations: src/llm/jsonSchema.ts:40 (own helper), :80 (Object.hasOwn for required), :82 (own() for the properties lookup), :131 and :134 (fromStrict uses own() and defineProperty).

reasoning:
Finding: "Replay: Reset during the Auto-play pause marks the next recorded step as played, so it is silently skipped later" (src/web/replay.ts). The cause: in play(), after the pause `await sleep(stepPauseMs)` between units, the code set `u.played = true` before checking the generation. A Reset during that pause had already cleared every played flag, so the stale loop marked the next unit of the new session as played. The fix in e4b6da3 (src/web/replay.ts:69-72) adds `if (gen !== this.generation) return;` straight after the pause and before `u.played = true`. Every other await in play() is followed by a generation check before any state changes (line 77, inside the event loop). After the last replay there is no await before `busy = undefined`, so a stale loop can no longer change the new generation's state. restart() clears busy, and a stale loop returns without touching it, so a new action after Reset is not blocked or cleared by the old loop.

I reproduced the scenario in throwaway worktrees at both commits, using a standalone test file. On b6304b7 the original scenario plays steps [0,2,3,4,5,6,6]: step 1 is skipped and step 6 plays twice. Variants tried on e4b6da3, all pass: Reset in the pause after step 3; two Resets in a row; Reset then pressing Next right away while the stale pause is still pending; Reset during Auto-play then Auto-play again. Variants 1 and 2 fail on old code, variants 3 and 4 pass on both.

The regression test is in test/web.test.ts ("reset during the pause between auto-played steps does not skip the next step", the replay describe block, about line 287 of the new file). So I ran the same test body as a standalone file against b6304b7's src, and it fails there, then passes on e4b6da3. variantsStillOpen: Concurrent merchant refunds still cause the bug. Two refundOrder calls in flight together (Promise.all) both pass the `if (o.refund)` guard before the PSP await at src/payments/sim/acpMerchant.ts:179-182. The first call sets status to returned. The second sees 'returned', which is neither shipped nor delivered, so line 189 sets it to 'refunded'. On e4b6da3 the order events end [created, shipped, delivered, returned, refunded] and trackOrder gives orderStatus=refunded, delivery.status=Cancelled, so the NonCompliant verdict is replaced. The PSP idempotency key refund:<order> means money is refunded only once (merchant balance 0); only the order status and verdict are wrong. A fix would be an in-flight per-order promise, like `completing` for checkout, or setting status from a snapshot taken before the await.

Minor, found by reading the code and not run: two concurrent buyer cancels of a 'created' order without an Idempotency-Key both reach refund() (acpMerchant.ts:226-235) before o.refund is set. Each pushes an event, so the order gets duplicate 'refunded' events. The final status is still 'refunded', so this is only cosmetic.
reasoning: Finding: a retried merchant refund flipped the order from 'returned' to 'refunded' and replaced the signed NonCompliant verdict with Cancelled (checkout variant). Cause at b6304b7: refund() always recomputed `o.status = shipped||delivered ? returned : refunded` (acpMerchant.ts:189). On a second call the status is already 'returned', so it became 'refunded' and a second event was pushed. Fix in e4b6da3 (commit 0631aaf): an early return `if (o.refund) return { status: 200, body: o };` at src/payments/sim/acpMerchant.ts:179, which covers both callers, refundOrder (line 287) and buyer cancel (line 235). I reproduced the original sequential scenario (deliver, NonCompliant verdict, refundOrder twice). It fails on b6304b7 and passes on e4b6da3. The regression test is the block added at the end of test 'a refund after delivery keeps the user's signed verdict and is recorded as a return' in test/checkout.test.ts:460-466. A buyer cancel after a return correctly gets 409 order_returned on both commits. The fix holds for sequential retries, which is the stated failure scenario, but a closely related concurrent variant is still open.
